newsitem.title: CHINA: China Eastern aims for 30 pct share list abroad.
newsitem.headline: China Eastern aims for 30 pct share list abroad.

text.p: China Eastern aims to become the first Chinese airline to list shares abroad, with the listing to account for about 30 percent of its total assets, a senior company official said on Tuesday.

Zhu Tonghai, senior executive and deputy head of the firm's Communist Party branch, said in an interview the precise timing of the listing depended on the state of the company's preparations and conditions in the markets involved.
The airline plans to list in New York and Hong Kong. A senior aviation official in Beijing said on Monday the dual listing should go ahead by the end of 1996.
"There is much work to do, on the use of land, valuation of assets, auditing of the balance sheets and agreement from the Bureau of Management of State Assets," Zhu said.
China Southern Airlines is now expected to list shares after China Eastern, probably early next year.
"Originally, both we and China Southern Airlines wanted to be the first to list abroad," he said.
He declined to give figures for China Eastern's profits, turnover or assets, but the company's 1995 annual report put 1995 revenue at 7 billion yuan and profits at about 500 million yuan.
In terms of number of planes, cargo and passenger volume, China Eastern ranks third in China, behind Air China and China Southern, he said.
In 1995, China Eastern carried 6.57 million passengers and 176,000 tonnes of cargo, up from 5.61 million and 149,000 tonnes in 1994, its 1995 annual report said.

Zhu said China Eastern had a debt-equity ratio of slightly more than 80 percent, with its domestic planes 70 percent full on average and domestic and international services each accounting for 50 percent of revenue.
The airline, set up in 1988, has more than 60 planes flying 127 domestic and foreign routes, he said.
